therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: ICOS agonism to enhance T-cell activation and proliferation
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: T-cell co-stimulation to enhance anti-tumor immune response in combination with PD-1 blockade
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: PD-L1 positive recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Overall survival and progression-free survival in PD-L1 CPS ≥1 and CPS ≥20 populations

subgroup_findings: Worse outcomes in high PD-L1 expressing tumors (CPS ≥20): OS HR 4.44 vs 1.51 in CPS ≥1
12-month OS rate: 46% vs 88% in CPS ≥20 population (feladilimab vs placebo arms)
safety_signals: Similar overall AE rates between arms (150/159 vs 145/156)
Fewer immune-related AEs with feladilimab: 49/159 vs 67/156
results.dose_information: Intravenous infusion, specific dosing not provided

context.duration: Up to approximately 16 months treatment, 43 months safety follow-up
